text: We evaluated a weak-to-strong generalization method that discards training examples where weak supervisors disagree, using a minimum agreement threshold of 0.8, on the SciQ testbed. Across num_seeds = 2 seeds, the method attained a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.95 with a standard error of 0.03. Taken at face value, this indicates that the strong student recovered most of the gap between the weak supervisor and the strong ceiling under this filtering scheme. Several caveats limit how far this should be read. No baseline PGR was supplied, so we cannot characterize the result as an improvement over naive weak supervision or any alternative filtering rule; the number stands alone. With only two seeds, the reported standard error rests on a very small sample and the spread across runs is poorly constrained. The finding is also specific to a single testbed and a single agreement threshold, so generalization to other datasets or thresholds remains untested here.
